title: The Little Book That Still Beats The Market

questions.q: What two metrics does Joel Greenblatt's magic formula rank companies by?
a: Earnings yield and return on capital
questions.why: The formula uses earnings yield and return on capital as the two ranking factors.

questions.q: How many years did Gotham Funds reportedly achieve over 40% annual returns?
questions.why: The overview notes 40% returns over a 20‑year period from 1986 to 2006.

questions.q: If a stock ranks 1st in earnings yield and 153rd in ROC, what combined rank does it receive?
questions.why: Combined rank is the sum of the two positions: 1 + 153 = 154.

questions.q: According to the book, how much would a $10,000 investment in 1988 be worth by 2009 using the formula?
questions.why: The text states $10,000 would grow to $1,000,000 by 2009.

questions.q: What behavior does the book say is essential for the formula's success?
a: Patience and staying out of new trouble
questions.why: The book stresses patience and avoiding new trouble as key to success.
